chunks: And through him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: 'Will the earth remain without an Imam?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'We narrate from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that it will not remain without an Imam except if Allah becomes angry with the people of the earth (or he said: with the servants).' He said: 'The earth will not remain without an Imam, and if it were to remain without one, it would sink.'

key_terms.أبو عبد الله: Abu Abdullah (referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إمام: Imam (divinely appointed leader and proof of God)
key_terms.الأرض: The earth (referring to the world of creation)

ai.seo_question: Why will the earth not remain without an Imam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Ra*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the cosmological necessity of the Imam, asserting that the earth cannot exist in a state of divine absence (*Ghaybat al-Imam*) without collapsing. He references the tradition of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to explain that while the earth might temporarily remain without an Imam during divine displeasure, it would ultimately 'sink' (*lasakhat*), highlighting the Imam as the sustaining pillar (*Hujjah*) of creation. This underscores the Shia doctrine that the Imam is not merely a political leader but the essential metaphysical anchor for the stability of the world.
